part: Regulations page composition — RegulationsLedger (real page component, not the ListSurfaceShell primitive)
source: dc.html p2 (#p2): masthead, band tiles, 'N regulations · grouped by band · Show as one list' + Sort row, rail (Filters card: MODE/JURISDICTION/TOPIC/SOURCE TIER, then 'Obligations · next 30 days', then Legend), band-sectioned rows. This spec exists per the operator's own complaint ('the filters were not above the regulations, they were on the right — same on every page; you are NOT matching the images directly') — it measures the COMPOSED page, not a shell primitive fed invented props, so a future regression that puts the facets back in the content column, or drops the sort row, or reorders the rail, is caught here.
notes: The pre-existing list-surface.json spec measures ListSurfaceShell/ListSurfaceRailCards in isolation via the 'list-surface-1440' mount (a minimal fixture: one facetGroup, no sortRow, no topic/tier). This spec measures the REAL RegulationsLedger composition (24-row fixture, matching capture-compose-lists-screenshots.mjs), so the sort row, the Topic/Source-tier facets, and the rail's actual top-to-bottom order are all exercised end to end.
Fixture is invented sample data with the real shape (same helper as the evidence screenshot); the audit asserts geometry/placement/labels, never fixture values.

The Filters rail card sits ABOVE the Legend rail card (p2's own top-to-bottom rail order) — asserted via a DOM-order sibling-combinator selector, since 'present but in the wrong place' was the exact original defect, not mere absence.

The rail's OBLIGATIONS · NEXT 30 DAYS card (lane comp-oblig, 2026-09-08) is measured here for presence, DOM order between Filters and Legend, its head label and 'Calendar →' link, and its four-row cap: artboard 02/id="p2" draws four dated rows, and the mount's obligation fixture deliberately includes a fifth event 90 days out so the card's own 30-day window is proven in the real composition, not only in obligation-rail-select.npmtest.mjs.

UI FIX ROUND 2026-09-08, items A1/A3 (lane cardrule): the rows named 'A1 rule on ...' and 'A3 shell of ...' below measure the card shell the operator ruled belongs to the CARD component. They assert the gradient's exact value, which the earlier rule rows on this page did not; the closing 'CLASS CLOSURE' row is the check that fails if any card on this page renders with no rule at all.

children.name: region 6a, the MODE facet reads the vocabulary's DISPLAY labels, title case as the artboard draws them
children.note: Artboard 02/id="p2" draws the FILTERS card's MODE rows as Air / Road / Ocean / Rail, title case, like its own JURISDICTION and TOPIC groups. The build printed the raw canonical token, so the group read 'air / ocean / road / rail' in lower case and was the only lower-case group in the card. Found by eye in train 60's visual pass; no spec measured it. The label now comes from TRANSPORT_MODES (the vocabulary that already owns it), and the option's `value` is untouched, so the stored/filtered token is still the canonical `ocean` of the 2026-08-12 ruling. This row asserts the DISPLAY form only. The match is a CASE-SENSITIVE substring, which is exactly the distinction under test: the lower-case token 'ocean' does not contain 'Ocean'. (Authoring note, fold 60: this row first used a `re:` regex with \b word boundaries and reported NOT BUILT against a correct product, because in JSON \b is the escape for BACKSPACE, so the parsed pattern searched for control characters. A regex in a spec file needs its backslashes doubled; a plain substring needs none, and is enough here.)

Measured before the fix: dot 6px, label letter-spacing .1em, window 10.5px; the label's size, weight, colour and casing were already correct. A2's three values differ from what artboard 02's own band-block header draws (8px dot, .1em label tracking, 11.5px window); the operator's 2026-09-08 item is the later ruling and wins over the artboard per the precedence rule, and both values are recorded in DEVIATION-LOG.md. A2 states nothing about the row's alignment or gap, so `align-items: baseline` and the 8px gap stay as they are (the artboard draws centre and 10px) and are logged rather than improvised. The band-coloured 3px rule above this header is correct today (ruling 5.2's one coloured rule per screen) and is untouched.

forbid.name: the MODE facet never prints a bare lower-case canonical token as a label
forbid.reason: The lower-case token is the storage form, not a label. Its reappearance here is exactly the regression this fold fixed, and it is invisible to every other row because the counts and the click behaviour are unchanged when only the case is wrong.

forbid.name: CLASS CLOSURE (regulations list): a card element that renders no 3px rule
forbid.reason: Coordinator note N3: 'Prove the class is closed ... a check that fails when a card element renders without it'. Encoded as a FORBID, which is the harness's own form for 'the design does not have this element': every card in the product is `SectionCard` (src/components/ui/SectionCard.tsx), which stamps `data-section-card` on itself and mounts the 3px rule in one of exactly two positions (its first flow child, or inside its own absolutely positioned wrapper when the card carries padding). This selector reaches a card with the rule in NEITHER position, so a match is a ruleless card and the row goes NOT IN SPEC. Ruling 5.2's band-grouping card, the one card that legitimately draws no dark-grey rule, stamps `data-section-card="band-grouping"` instead, so it is outside this selector by identity rather than by being invisible to it.
